newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian policemen freed in Chechnya -- agencies.
newsitem.headline: Russian policemen freed in Chechnya -- agencies.

text.p: A group of 21 Russian policemen seized by Chechen fighters loyal to field commander Salman Raduyev were released on Wednesday after four days in captivity, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Tass, quoting the interior ministry of the Dagestan region which borders Chechnya, said the policemen had been handed over in the settlement of Gerzel-Kutan at 3.30 p.m. (1230 GMT). The agency gave no further details.
Raduyev, who led a bloody hostage-taking raid in the southern Russian city of Budennovsk last year, seized the policemen after they refused to allow his men to enter Dagestan.

He said on Tuesday he wanted apologies from Russia for not letting him into Dagestan and could kill his hostages if anyone tried to free them by force. Russian officials have been in the region to try to negotiate an end to the seizure.

The separatist leadership in the breakaway republic, keen not to upset a fragile peace process and anxious to present a united front, had promised to force Raduyev to release all his hostages unconditionally.
